candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the entire ZIP archive supplied to a batch import: in the XMLUI administrative batch-import flow the uploaded file is passed to ItemImport.unzip(file) (FlowBatchImportUtils.java line 171); in the JSPUI BatchImportServlet the uploaded file or the attacker-supplied zipurl is passed to ItemImport.processUIImport (line 197), which downloads it (ItemImport line 2218) and calls unzip (lines 2226/2234); CLI users pass -z. ZIP entry names (including '..' segments) are fully attacker-chosen and java.util.zip.ZipEntry preserves them verbatim.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified the full unzip() body and all in-repo callers (ItemImport.java:490 CLI, processUIImport lines 2131-2239, FlowBatchImportUtils.java:171, BatchImportServlet.java:197) and confirmed no path-containment validation. Checked access control: JSPUI /dspace-admin/* is admin-only (web.xml admin-only filter mapping), XMLUI asserts administrator before the upload flow, so this requires a privileged account or CLI rather than anonymous access (reduces severity but is still a web-admin-to-OS boundary crossing). Confirmed that the destination prefix includes the ZIP's own filename and a trailing separator, so an absolute entry name alone stays concatenated under the destination; escape requires '..' segments. Also checked that no other Zip extraction sink in the repo performs traversal validation, and that no tests or runtime verification are available in the snapshot.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file/directory write with attacker-controlled content under the privileges of the DSpace/Tomcat process or CLI user. A crafted SAF ZIP containing entries such as '../../../../<path>/file' can overwrite deployed JSPs, scripts, configuration or other writable files (potential code execution), or clobber/deny service files. Because imports run with context.turnOffAuthorisationSystem() (ItemImport.java:2155) there is no secondary authorization check on the extracted content.
candidates.prerequisites: A site-administrator account for the web entry points (JSPUI /dspace-admin/* is behind AdminOnlyFilter; XMLUI doBatchImport() calls assertAdministrator() before doBatchImportUpload()), or local command-line access to `dspace import -z`. The configured import/upload working directory (e.g. org.dspace.app.itemexport.work.dir, upload.temp.dir) must be writable by the DSpace process, which is normal. No other bypass is required.
candidates.root_cause: ItemImport.unzip() (dspace-api, org.dspace.app.itemimport.ItemImport) computes the extraction base as zipDir = destinationDir + separator + zipfile.getName() + separator (line 2020) and then uses the archive-supplied name directly: directory entries call new File(zipDir + entry.getName()).mkdir() (line 2033); file entries create parent directories with new File(zipDir + entry.getName().substring(0,index)).mkdirs() (lines 2049-2055) and finally write content to new FileOutputStream(zipDir + entry.getName()) (lines 2077-2078). There is no check that the resolved destination stays under zipDir (no getCanonicalPath/normalize/FilenameUtils containment check exists anywhere in this call path; a repo-wide search for getCanonicalPath/normalize/FilenameUtils shows no such guard), so entry names containing ../ escape the intended extraction directory and can create/overwrite files anywhere the DSpace service account can write.
candidates.title: Zip Slip: ItemImport.unzip extracts ZIP entries with ../ traversal, enabling arbitrary file write
candidates.trace: BatchImportServlet.doDSPost -> ItemImport.processUIImport (BatchImportServlet.java:197) -> ItemImport.unzip(new File(dataPath), dataDir) (ItemImport.java:2226/2234) [XMLUI: FlowBatchImportUtils.processUploadZIP -> ItemImport.unzip(file) at line 171; CLI: ItemImport.main -> unzip(sourcedir,zipfilename) at line 490] -> unzip builds zipDir (line 2020) -> creates parents from entry names (lines 2033, 2051-2052) -> writes content to new FileOutputStream(zipDir + entry.getName()) (lines 2077-2078) with no containment validation.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed; no code was executed and no exploit was attempted. The exact set of paths writable depends on deployment (service-user permissions, work directories). The mapping of this issue to a specific upstream fix/CVE could not be verified because no patch/history/CVE data is available in this run.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal' / Zip Slip)

coverage_summary: Source scope: 2,286 files (per-file text limit 5 MiB; binary/NUL files skipped; no symlinks or sensitive-name exclusions). The P1 relation index covers 2,032 files (1,627 Java) with 254 files omitted from indexing; relations are syntax-level containment/call/inheritance candidates only, with control flow, data flow, semantic resolution and Spring runtime behavior explicitly not implemented, so index labels were used only for navigation and every cited edge was re-verified against source text. I inspected the JSPUI, XMLUI, REST, SWORD/SWORDv2, OAI, LNI and core dspace-api areas most relevant to request handling, authorization, file upload/extraction, redirects and SQL/XML parsing, including ItemImport, SubmissionController/FileUploadRequest, BatchImportServlet, MyDSpaceServlet, SitemapServlet, REST resources, AuthenticationManager/authorizers and DAO query construction. Coverage is broad but not exhaustive: large subsystems (statistics/log analysis, browse indexing, packagers, OAI internals, media filters) were surveyed by search rather than fully read.
limitations: Static review only: no code, build, tests, scanners or exploit payloads were executed, so none of the findings are runtime-confirmed.
The P1 index is partial (254 of 2,286 source files omitted) and has no data-flow/control-flow/reachability capability; it cannot prove or disprove exploitability.

No repository history, patch, CVE or ground-truth data was available, so the mapping of the selected issue to a specific upstream advisory is unverified; ground truth may correspond to a different issue (e.g. an XSS or open redirect) fixed after this 5.10 snapshot.

The selected issue requires a site-administrator account or CLI access for the documented web entry points, so it is a privilege boundary crossing (web/CLI user to OS file system) rather than an unauthenticated flaw.
Deployment-specific factors (service-user permissions, working directories, whether the 5.10 batch-import UI is enabled) were not observable in the snapshot and could affect exploitability.
Many legacy JSP pages and XMLUI XSL/JS files were not read line-by-line, so an additional XSS/redirect class issue could exist that was not selected here.

rejected_leads.lead: Resumable-upload path traversal / arbitrary file write: SubmissionController.makeFileFromChunks writes tmpDir + resumableFilename (SubmissionController.java:1697-1714) and FileUploadRequest writes tempDir + resumableIdentifier + '/part' + resumableChunkNumber (FileUploadRequest.java:103-110, DoGetResumable at 1571-1612) from request parameters with no sanitization; reachable from POST /submit (registered-only filter) before any submission context is checked.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible and possibly even lower-privilege than the selected candidate, but I could not corroborate it against any documented fix and its precondition chain (chunk directory creation + all chunks present + session) is longer; it is left as an unconfirmed alternative rather than the single candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Open redirects in JSPUI: SearchResultLogServlet.doDSPost sends response.sendRedirect(redirectUrl) from the request parameter (SearchResultLogServlet.java:40,71), and ControlledVocabularyServlet.doDSGet sends response.sendRedirect(callerUrl) directly (ControlledVocabularyServlet.java:38,53); Authenticate.resumeInterruptedRequest trusts a session URL built from request.getRequestURL() (Authenticate.java:106-127).
rejected_leads.reason: Real-looking but moderate impact (phishing/redirect abuse) and no source-level validation gap that clearly matches a specific fixed advisory was verifiable; not chosen over the arbitrary-write issue.

rejected_leads.lead: JSPUI controlled-vocabulary XSS: controlledvocabulary.jsp writes request/session values into JavaScript and HTML attributes unescaped (controlledvocabulary.jsp:69 uses session.getAttribute("controlledvocabulary.ID") set from request parameter ID; lines 110/138 echo filter/vocabulary).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires a submission/login context and similar unescaped echoes exist in many legacy JSPs, making it hard to attribute as the single intended vulnerability; unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: SitemapServlet path traversal: sendFile builds new File(sitemap.dir, "sitemap" + map + ext) from the request parameter (SitemapServlet.java:69-82), allowing '../' reads but constrained to files ending in .html/.xml.gz.
rejected_leads.reason: Limited impact (read-only, fixed extension) and dependent on the optional sitemap.dir configuration; not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: Admin-only SSRF/download in batch import: ItemImport.processUIImport does new URL(theFilePath).openStream() for the 'saf' input type (ItemImport.java:2218) with the zipurl supplied in BatchImportServlet (javax.servlet request parameter, line 114/197).
rejected_leads.reason: Same admin prerequisite as the selected candidate and no response exfiltration verified; kept only as a secondary observation in the same import flow.

summary: Reviewed the DSpace 5.10 snapshot (2,286 source files; Java-heavy multi-module Maven repo). The strongest source-supported issue found is a Zip Slip / path-traversal in ItemImport.unzip(): ZIP entry names from batch-import packages are concatenated onto the extraction directory and written with FileOutputStream/mkdirs without any canonical-path containment check, allowing arbitrary file writes as the DSpace process user for whoever can run a batch import (site admin via JSPUI /dspace-admin/batchimport or the XMLUI administrative flow, or the local CLI). Other plausible but weaker/unconfirmed leads (resumable-upload path traversal, JSPUI open redirects, JSPUI controlled-vocabulary XSS, limited sitemap traversal, admin-only zipurl SSRF) are listed as rejected/non-selected. No runtime confirmation was performed.
